scanlineOverText.ask: Jac: 'make sure the scan lines sit atop the text.'
scanlineOverText.why: A glass film physically covers everything behind it, text included. In CSS the film is a background-image on the board element, so it sits BEHIND the element's own text — Figma lets us do the more convincing thing.
scanlineOverText.how: The film is lifted out of the glass fill stack into its OWN layer, same cavity geometry, inserted directly above the label (above the glass when a variant has no label) and below the ring core — the ring is frame edge, not under glass. Removed from the glass stack so it cannot paint twice.
scanlineOverText.stillSwitched: The film's opacity is bound to finish/glass-opacity, same as the glass holder, so both turn off together.
scanlineOverText.layerOrder: well · plate · inner · glass (tier-01) · [label] · scanline film · glow · ring core

fillState.ask: Jac: full red starting from INSIDE the red outlines, ink turns white, red must stay translucent enough to still see the Halo Circuit asset.
fillState.build: a 'fill (state/hot-fill)' layer on the cavity's own octagon, above the glass and below the label, at 70% NODE opacity. Layer order: well · plate · inner · glass · fill · label · scanline film · glow · ring core — so the film still rides over both the fill and the text.
fillState.inkIsNotPureWhite: binds to the new ink/on-fill semantic — CANON #fdfdfd, MOCKUP #f4f9fa. Canon deepened --red-fill to #d63636 AND pinned a near-white ink because white on #ff4242 measures 3.44 and fails AA (ledger #3). Hardcoding #fff would have reintroduced exactly the failure canon fixed.
fillState.opacityGotcha: PAINT-level opacity did not survive being spread onto a bound paint object — it read back as 1 and the fill was fully opaque, hiding the circuit completely, which was the one thing Jac specified. Set opacity on the NODE instead. Verified by reading the value back, not by eye.
fillState.tuning: 0.86 -> 0.82 -> 0.70. Below ~0.75 the hex field reads as darker patches through the red; above it the circuit vanishes. 0.70 is a judgement point, easily changed on the four fill layers.

Bracket.domOrderIsLoadBearing: The divider MUST paint before vertical/tip/elbow — the elbow's painted extent far exceeds its declared 43x5.6 rect and overlaps the divider's left end. Reversing it is a measured defect (max delta 176 at canvas x52..60, y228..234).
Bracket.tipMask: A horizontal alpha ramp eating the first 2px and feathering the last 2. Figma paints have NO DESTINATION_OUT blend, so it is a real alpha mask node.
Bracket.elbow: rotate(43.5deg) about transform-origin 0 50% with margin-top:-2.8px, as a relativeTransform matrix.
Bracket.assemblyTrap: c10's .bt-warm paints AFTER this bracket and fully occludes the elbow in canvas column x33..37, so the bracket is NOT one contiguous layer relative to c10 — something from c10 must interleave at assembly time.

Marks.arialSubstitution: Arial is NOT in Figma; Arimo IS, and it is metrically compatible with Arial by design (identical advance widths). marks.css picked Arial specifically 'to match measured glyph widths', so the metrics ARE the requirement — Arimo preserves exactly that, where any other grotesque would keep the look and break the measurement.
Marks.rivetCentreDropped: The radial is specified at 'circle at 50% 45%'; on a 9px dot that is 0.45px above centre, below one pixel, so the default centred transform is used.
Marks.hexIsMeasured: stroke #6f3d22 is close to but NOT --amber (#7c401f) — measured, stays baked. The name binds to ink/bright.

Deck.hardStopBandCounts: bt-face 37, bt-right 34, bt-slate 36, bt-well 73, bt-warm 86 — each colour emitted TWICE at both band edges or Figma interpolates the hard stop away
Deck.wellGrid: 1px rules every 9.4px — a NON-INTEGER period, so it cannot be a plain tile. Drawn at 5x where the period is an exact 47px, as a 235px PNG scaled back by 0.20. imageHash 0c605bad4b35c27bb6b1c89d5321e1b7bdd4ae50.
Deck.notReproduced: The grid's background-position 3px 9px offset — Figma image tiles have no offset control.
Deck.slateMask: linear-gradient(90deg,#000 0 50%,transparent 100%) as a real alpha mask node.
Deck.btRightIsAHoleFiller: Not an independent feature — it is the face strip left exposed by c1's PROMISED chip and is shaped by that chip, so it only makes sense in assembly.
Deck.rivetHalfPixel: x=0.5 is MEASURED, not rounding. Its own gate cannot prove it: c12's loose rivet #4 covers all but a 2-row sliver in assembly (max delta 1), so it is correct by construction.

decisions.oneLanguageCollection: Colour, type and finish semantics all live in ONE collection (Halo Language), so flipping MOCKUP↔CANON is a single mode switch — the plan's scope-lock goal (FIGMA-PLAN.md 0d).
decisions.mockupIsDefaultMode: MOCKUP is mode 1, the default every new frame inherits. Components are built byte-exact against the mockup, so Phase 3 screenshot validation must render the mockup skin.
decisions.geometryCollectionRemoved: Created in P1.a, found to have no legitimate content, removed in P1.h. This kit has NO shared geometry scale — every part carries its own measured geometry. Per-part knobs become Figma COMPONENT PROPERTIES in Phase 3, not variables. Canon's control ladder exists but governs canon UI and is self-conflicted (ledger #140 reverses #131).
decisions.noEffectStyles: No foundations-level effect styles. Each part's blur radii are measured individually; there is no shared glow ladder to name. Per-part effects land with their components in Phase 3.
decisions.gapsAreVisibleNotHidden: Where canon has no locked value (metal/silver, all four rim tones, ground/cavity, ground/circuit, ground/edge, ground/maroon, ground/maroon-d, and the whole emissive/* family), CANON aliases the MOCKUP primitive and the variable description says so in the file.
decisions.emissiveNamespace: The mockup's six-strong emissive red family is namespaced emissive/* because that family IS the glow identity canon rejects — naming it that way makes the one non-swappable difference legible.
decisions.textStyleSizes: The 7 text styles use canon's locked ladder (28/15/13/12/11/10/9.5) — the only locked type scale in the project. The mockup's sizes are measured fits and are deliberately absent; they are set per-component in Phase 3.
decisions.chosenNotFound: Stamped tracking = 4%, the MIDDLE of canon's stated 0.03–0.06em range. A chosen point, not a found one — flagged in every style description. line-height left AUTO because canon specifies none.
decisions.inkAmendment: Phase 1 shipped with NO ink semantic (skipped because the mockup has no text-colour token). Caught in Phase 2 before anything was built on the gap. The kit's real inks were traced to source — chip.css:274 #f2585a, screen.css:103 #f4595a, marks.css:155 #f4f9fa, etch.css:225 rgba(150,185,205,.66) — and became 4 primitives + 4 mode-aware ink/* semantics scoped TEXT_FILL. ink-label and ink-readout differ by two steps and were deliberately NOT merged: the kit is byte-exact, so near-identical values stay distinct.
decisions.modePinnedColumns: The Foundations page shows MOCKUP and CANON side by side as two frames with setExplicitVariableModeForCollection overrides, rather than one frame the reader has to flip. The CANON column is a clone() of the MOCKUP column, so the two are provably identical geometry and only the mode differs.
decisions.chipFirstInPhase3: Jac, 2026-08-03: 'not that concerned about those colors, it will change with signal.' The Halo Chip IS canon's Signal archetype (the state you read), so Chip moves to FIRST in the Phase 3 order. The plan's original order was ascending node count, not a dependency chain, so nothing blocks the move.

openGaps: No line-height locked for any step of canon's type ladder — text styles left AUTO.
No letter-spacing locked for Archivo (only the mono voice's ~0.03–0.06em range).
--accent-line is named in wrangler-style (focus rings) but has no hex or formula anywhere.
--red-line is a color-mix() derivation, not a static hex — cannot be a Figma primitive as-is.
No general spacing/padding scale exists in canon; only the 24px control height and the type ladder.
43 primitives carry no description (not required; they are hidden from pickers).

conduitSimplification.ask: Jac: 'doesnt need so many gradients and components for it to feel real'
conduitSimplification.result: 559 -> 359 stops, 41.7KB -> 28.4KB, visually indistinguishable. All 19 layers named; light channel halo bound to emissive/tube-red inside a glow container bound to finish/glow-opacity.
conduitSimplification.method: ERROR-BOUNDED ADAPTIVE simplification — drop a stop only where removal shifts the curve <10/255 on any channel. Measured ceiling: TOL 4 -> 20% fewer, 6 -> 27%, 10 -> 36%. Only ~a quarter of the stops are redundant; the rest encode real shading.
conduitSimplification.whyItCannotGoFurther: The SVG is a MACHINE TRACE of a raster (stops at 3.33%, 6.67%, 9.52% — no designer chose those), so the detail is baked photographic shading, not design intent.
twoFailedAttempts: Cherry-picked dark/mid/light stops spread evenly AND dropped stop-opacity — narrow highlights became broad opaque washes, the whole part came out pink. Always carry alpha.
Uniform resampling at 7 even points — this art is high-frequency (2px highlight next to near-black), so uniform downsampling smears exactly the detail that makes it read as steel.
conduitSimplification.ifFewerSHAPESareWanted: Not a compression problem. The honest route is AUTHORING the conduit as real geometry (~8 shapes, 3-5 stops each) — a cleaner, less photographic look. That is a redesign, not a simplification.
conduitSimplification.status: Jac is hand-editing the elbow; Claude to review later.

calibrationAgainstSource.why: Slots' blur LOOKED wrong in Figma and the instinct was to reduce it. Rendering the actual source with Playwright and comparing like-for-like at 4x showed the Figma build was already correct — the reference eye was tier-01's crisp slot ticks, which are a DIFFERENT design. 'Fixing' it would have broken a correct component.
calibrationAgainstSource.method: scratchpad/render-slots.mjs serves docs/design/halo-elements on :9147 and screenshots the part's own selector at deviceScaleFactor 4 with a margin for skew/blur spill; then capture the Figma variant at the same scale, margin and background colour.
calibrationAgainstSource.rule: Before adjusting any measured value because it 'looks off', render the source and compare at matched scale. The kit has a byte-exact source for every part — there is never a reason to judge by memory.

transformsAndBlur.skew: Figma has NO skew property. skewX(A) about transform-origin 50%/50% goes in as relativeTransform [[1, tanA, x - tanA*h/2], [0, 1, y]] — the tx term pulls the centre back, which is what the 50% origin means. Used by Slots (18deg).
transformsAndBlur.blur: CSS filter blur(Npx) is a Gaussian stdDeviation; Figma's LAYER_BLUR radius reads about 2x that. blur(1.4px) -> radius 2.8 and blur(.81) -> 1.62 both verified against source renders.
transformsAndBlur.clipsThatMustNotBeSquared: Slots Row=B clips a canvas-space box whose LEFT edge is at -30. Pulling that to 0 (the obvious frame-clip) would shave the leftmost bar's own skew+blur spill, which reaches ~-2.2 local. The clip frame is offset to x=-30 width=281 so the right cut still lands at 251.

gradientTraps.offBoxStops: Housing's .face declares stops at 251px and 253px on a box only 248px tall (top:5 bottom:1 on a 254 root), so CSS never paints them. Figma positions must be 0-1, and clamping those stops to 1.0 COMPRESSES and distorts the ramp. Correct handling: drop the off-box stops and interpolate the true colour at the box edge — here #28303a, 25% of the way from #1d242e(247) to #47535d(251). Check every multi-stop gradient for stops beyond its own paint box.
gradientTraps.hardStopBands: CSS '#303232 0 1px' is a SOLID band, not a gradient point. Figma smooth-interpolates between stops, which erases the band. Emit each colour TWICE — at position i/n and (i+1)/n — to hold the hard edge. Used by Housing's rim-l (6 bands) and rim-r (5 bands).

figmaGotchas.opacityVariablesArePercent: An OPACITY-scoped FLOAT variable resolves as a PERCENTAGE (0-100), NOT 0-1. finish/glow-opacity was first stored as 1 and rendered as 1%, silently switching the mockup's glow off in BOTH modes — and the screenshot still looked plausible. Correct values: MOCKUP=100, CANON=0.
figmaGotchas.nestedOpacityMultiplies: A node cannot carry both a bound opacity and its own measured opacity. The chip's bloom has a per-variant measured opacity (1/.95/.55/.55) AND must be glow-suppressed, so the glow layers are NESTED in a container whose opacity carries the token. Nested opacity multiplies, so both survive.
figmaGotchas.querySelectorSpaces: node.query('VECTOR[name=ring core]') does NOT match — a space in an attribute value breaks the selector and returns empty, which reads as 'node missing' rather than 'bad query'. Use children.find(c => c.name === '...') for names containing spaces.
figmaGotchas.createAutoLayoutWhiteFill: figma.createAutoLayout() frames arrive with an opaque WHITE fill. Any layout-only frame needs fills = [] or it paints a white slab.
figmaGotchas.textStyleBindingsResolveInDefaultMode: A text style with a bound fontFamily reports its concrete face resolved in the file's DEFAULT mode, not the face you assigned. That is correct behaviour, not a failed write.
figmaGotchas.loadTheNodesCURRENTfonts: Mutating .characters on a node whose fontFamily is BOUND to a variable throws 'Cannot write to node with unloaded font' naming the face the variable RESOLVES to — not the face you assigned. Renaming a Text/Title 15 node threw on Roboto Bold because type/body-family resolves to Roboto in MOCKUP. Load every face any mode could resolve to.
figmaGotchas.svgPathSyntax: figma vectorPaths rejects the compact 'M13.5,2.3L126.6,2.3' form with 'Invalid command'. Normalise to space-separated: d.replace(/([MLZmlz])/g,' $1 ').replace(/,/g,' ').
figmaGotchas.appendedChildrenLandOnTop: appendChild puts a node LAST = topmost. The Message Board's glass layer covered the label and ring until it was moved with insertChild(innerIdx+1, holder). Always read the child order back after building.
figmaGotchas.noDestinationOut: Figma paint blendModes do NOT include DESTINATION_OUT (or any Porter-Duff compositing). A CSS mask-image has to become a real alpha mask node — a child with isMask=true whose own alpha drives visibility.

conduitSegments.method: 9 real segments (head bar, two feet, legs, diagonal run, vertical run, two elbow blocks, end plate), each ONE 5-stop cross-section gradient — deep, body, NARROW crown, body, deep — plus INNER_SHADOW bevels and a TEXTURE grain doing the depth work that 19 traced polygons were doing before. The lit core binds to emissive/tube-red with a LAYER_BLUR halo in a finish/glow-opacity container. Source clipPath kept verbatim as a mask.

figmaEffectSupportProbed.note: Probed by attempting each on a throwaway node and catching the validation error — worth re-running rather than assuming, since the set changes.

conduitSegments.whatMadeTheFirstPassLookWrong: A 3-stop gradient with the crown at 42% spans half of each segment and reads as chrome. The trace's realism is a NARROW specular band on a near-black body, so the crown needs to be a thin stop with dark on both sides.
conduitSegments.status: Alternative offered, not substituted — Jac chooses which becomes canonical.

capabilityProbe_2026_08_03.method: Probed by attempting each property/effect on a throwaway node and catching the validation error, plus list_shader_fills / list_shader_effects against the account library. Re-run rather than trusting this record — the surface changes.

strokes.note: Brush and Dynamic strokes are Figma Draw UI features. No `brush`/`strokeBrush`/`strokeWeightProfile` key exists on VectorNode, so they CANNOT be scripted — Jac can apply them by hand, Claude cannot generate them. Verified with `in` checks against the prototype chain (Object.keys on a node proxy returns nothing and is NOT a valid test).

biggestImplications: Fractal noise + Pattern grid shader FILLS are procedural — they can replace the tiled scanline/grain IMAGE assets currently on the glass layer, removing raster dependencies entirely.

Gradient map shader EFFECT maps luminance to a configurable ramp. This is a candidate answer to the standing CANON limitation (hundreds of measured gradient stops are baked, so CANON is token-layer only) — a luminance remap could reskin baked shading without dual-baking every stop. Needs testing; shader params may not be variable-bindable per mode.
effectStyles is currently EMPTY — every shadow/blur in the library is inline, so there is no single place to retune 'the well press' or 'the glow'.

shaderFillTest.detail: SHADER paints want {type:'SHADER', id}. But figma.importShaderById rejects the account-library id, and figma.listAvailableShaders() returns 0 in this file. The nine shader fills exist in Jac's account library and are reachable from the Figma UI, but the plugin API sees an empty shader registry.
shaderFillTest.correctsEarlierReport: The 2026-08-03 capability report listed shader fills as an opportunity Claude could drive. It is not, as things stand. Untested next step: if Jac applies a shader fill by hand once, it may register in the file and become visible to listAvailableShaders — worth checking before relying on it.
